name: Extend Finset probabilistic framework to infinite spaces via MeasureTheory

insights: Linearity of expectation is just integral_add in MeasureTheory (one-liner!)
Counting measure gives uniform distribution on finite types
First moment method needs Markov's inequality + integrability
knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Bridge from Finset to MeasureTheory. Proved linearity + indicator expectation.

problemStatement.formal: Bridge finite uniform expectation to MeasureTheory integrals and prove first-moment and linearity-of-expectation statements for probability measures.
problemStatement.plain: Extends the probabilistic-method expectation entry from finite `Finset` sums into Mathlib's measure-theoretic integral framework. The file shows counting measure gives the finite uniform model, equates finite expectation with an integral, proves a first-moment method statement, and records linearity of expectation as `integral_add`.
whyMatters: Many probabilistic-method arguments start as finite sums but become cleaner when phrased with measure-theoretic expectation.
The bridge lets finite combinatorial probability results reuse Mathlib integration tools.
First-moment and linearity statements are basic building blocks for future probabilistic combinatorics entries.

proven: `counting_measure_is_uniform` connects counting measure on a finite type to uniform total mass.
`finset_expectation_eq_integral` proves the finite average equals the integral against the uniform counting probability measure.
`first_moment_method` proves that expectation below one forces positive mass on the zero fiber for natural-valued random variables.
`linearity_of_expectation` records expectation linearity from `integral_add`, and `expectation_indicator` identifies indicator expectation with event probability.
open: The current OQ01 file is complete; broader infinite-space probabilistic-method applications are left to future entries.
knownResults.goal: Document the completed Finset-to-MeasureTheory expectation bridge.
